scope: Actual ICRSP Commentaires paragraphs inspected at distinct source URLs, separate from automated lexical matches; observations are what the host says, NOT original edition attestation or user-facing approved historical facts.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The website connects Thursday of Easter Octave to newly baptized Christians, a station at the Twelve Apostles, Philip and the Ethiopian, and the Resurrection appearances.
rows.publicationGate: Check distinct biblical readings and 1962 station/canonical Mass ID; do not infer universal posture or copy translated Proper.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The page explicitly calls this a pre-1955 Sacred Heart Octave, explains its 1955 suppression, and includes later John Paul II catechesis as editorial supplementation.
rows.publicationGate: Never display as a 1962 octave; distinguish later papal words and copyright from older liturgical commentary.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The website describes Friday of Advent Ember Days and a special December 21 St Thomas concurrence, together with Visitation references in the historical Office.
rows.publicationGate: Compare actual 1962 precedence, orations, and weekday computation; website quotation is not independently authenticated rubric.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The historical note traces Timothy's January 24 feast entry and changes in pre-1962 liturgical rank; Guéranger relates him to Paul and Ephesus.
rows.publicationGate: Require exact saint ID and independent death/date evidence; do not make historical ranks present 1962 rubrics.

rows.sourceTitle: St Grégoire le Grand, pape, confesseur et docteur
rows.observedEditorialSubject: The source names Gregory's March 12 commemoration and historical cult, and later catechetical discussion treats his Pastoral Rule and scriptural exegesis.
rows.publicationGate: Check authored layers: Guéranger, modern papal material and historical source notes cannot be presented as single Gregory quotation.

rows.sourceTitle: St Cyrille de Jérusalem, évêque, confesseur et docteur
rows.observedEditorialSubject: The website juxtaposes the March 18 feast with a reported April 18 death and relates Cyril's catechetical work to Lenten baptismal preparation.
rows.publicationGate: Check death and actual calendar dates against independent primary historical evidence; distinguish old feast rank and newer designation.

rows.sourceTitle: Commun des Apôtres et Évangélistes hors du temps pascal
rows.sourceSectionLocator: Présentation / Pius Parsch Le bréviaire expliqué
rows.observedEditorialSubject: The page explains the Apostles and Evangelists Common in the Roman Breviary and contrasts an older vigils calendar with post-1960 observances.
rows.publicationGate: Primarily Divine Office material, not a license to alter the 1962 Mass Commons form; edition boundaries held.

rows.sourceTitle: Commun de la Dédicace d’une église
rows.observedEditorialSubject: Parsch interprets church dedication through the stone church, the Church as Christ's spouse, and the sanctified Christian soul.
rows.publicationGate: Source theological commentary only. Any original full quotation requires edition attribution/translation rights and exact Mass Common identity.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The source specifies a Dec 14 regional observance associated with Alsace and presents Odile's family, monastery and healing-at-baptism tradition.
rows.publicationGate: Do not treat miracles or hagiographic narrative as independently verified biography; confirm local diocesan jurisdiction, artwork and actual saint ID.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The webpage explicitly distinguishes Joseph Cafasso's supplemental 1962 Missal entry from the general Roman calendar and mentions his priestly formation and influence on Don Bosco.
rows.publicationGate: Verify universal-versus-supplement legal scope and saint birth/death detail before any feast addition.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The source organizes Christmas into Midnight, Dawn, and Day Mass commentaries and different Office segments; one article thus contains multiple distinct proper contexts.
rows.publicationGate: Do not map one URL to one Mass form or merge all three Proper texts; original source author work dates and Office/Mass ownership must be separated.

rows.sourceTitle: St Etienne (26 décembre, 2ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de la Nativité)
rows.observedEditorialSubject: The page discusses December 26 St Stephen alongside Nativity and quotes older liturgical homilies contrasting Christ's birth with the first martyr's triumph.
rows.publicationGate: Historical claims about first attested martyr death dates and discovery/reception of relics need independent source review; distinguish attributed homilies.

rows.sourceTitle: 4ᵉ jour dans l’Octave de St Jean-Baptiste (avant 1955)
rows.observedEditorialSubject: The source expressly places the June 27 John Baptist octave day before 1955 and describes interaction with the Precious Blood feast historically.
rows.publicationGate: Never reinstate abolished 1955 octave as a 1962 universal day; separate old 1908/1955 sources from current scope.

rows.sourceTitle: St Laurent de Brindes, Confesseur et Docteur
rows.observedEditorialSubject: The page gives the 1959 Doctor of the Church declaration, July 21 Roman feast context, and separate 2011 papal catechesis carrying copyright notice.
rows.publicationGate: Distinguish St Lawrence of Brindisi from the Roman deacon St Lawrence in later embedded material; no copying ©2011 Vatican catechesis.

rows.sourceTitle: Commun des Fêtes de la bienheureuse Vierge Marie
rows.sourceSectionLocator: Présentation / Pius Parsch Le bréviaire expliqué
rows.observedEditorialSubject: The text explains the Marian Breviary Common and how Common Offices supply material when a feast lacks a complete proper Office.
rows.publicationGate: Breviary context only; do not create a new Office app module or misassign office propers to Mass Common.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The local page associates St Gengoult with Toul/Lorraine and narrates a medieval marriage-and-martyrdom legend including a miraculous water ordeal.
rows.publicationGate: Hagiographic episodes not independently historical; avoid repeating punitive miracle narrative without context; verify saint feast scope.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The page states the Apostles' vigil Mass form was abolished under the 1955 rubrical simplification, though it also retains older explanatory commentary.
rows.publicationGate: Explicit historical exception. Never present obsolete Vigil of Apostles as 1962 Mass; check equivalence with a0304_ancien.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The Ego autem Apostles Vigil page reproduces substantially similar introductory and Parsch explanations to a0045_nouveau under a distinct article ID.
rows.publicationGate: Possible duplicated source body: verify normalized source hash and specific form ID before de-dup; both are obsolete for 1962.

rows.sourceTitle: Commun des Vierges III : pour une Vierge Dilexísti
rows.observedEditorialSubject: Schuster-labelled source interprets Psalm 44 and virginity as bridal/mystical ecclesial imagery in the Mass Common for a Virgin.
rows.publicationGate: Do not equate editorial Scripture allegory with direct canonical prophecy; confirm precise Common formulary and source translator rights.

rows.observedEditorialSubject: The source presents a local Marian shrine story in Nancy, a claimed 1525 miracle and damage to the statue, and a 1955 move from local feast to votive Mass.
rows.publicationGate: Verify precise Nancy/Toul jurisdiction, statue provenance, report-of-miracle status, 1955 proper legal scope and shrine identity; no public new venue based only on text.
